name: RustFS
tagline: An S3-compatible object storage system written in Rust.
hook: A layered guide to instruction precedence, permission-gated actions, verification tiers, storage rules, and review evidence.
summary: RustFS states which instructions win, what actions need permission, and how much verification each change requires before reaching storage rules. Reviews need evidence, with stricter steps for adversarial validation and focused references for specific tasks.

techniques.title: Keep local invariants distinct from shared workflow
techniques.body: The nearest instruction file wins on domain invariants, but scoped guidance cannot replace the root verification tiers with a generic workspace gate. The file also says that skills cannot expand user authorization.
techniques.quote:
Nested instructions add to ancestor rules; they do not discard non-conflicting
rules. A skill cannot expand the user's requested scope or grant authorization.

techniques.title: Scale verification to the final diff
techniques.body: Documentation, non-behavioral source edits, localized behavior changes, and broad cross-module changes have different checks. Broader gates are conditional, and successful umbrella checks should not be duplicated.
techniques.quote:
Select checks from the final task-owned diff. Scoped `AGENTS.md` files may add a
concrete path-specific check, but must not replace this tiering with a generic
full-workspace gate.

techniques.title: Permit a review with no findings
techniques.body: The review guidance rejects a finding quota and requires checking callers, invariants, and tests for counterevidence. Missing tests are described as verification gaps rather than proof of a runtime defect.
techniques.quote:
A review has no finding quota; `No findings` is a complete outcome. A request to
find problems is not evidence that a defect exists.

techniques.title: Keep transient plans out of the durable knowledge base
techniques.body: One-shot plans and benchmark snapshots are distinguished from architecture, operations, and testing references. A named script enforces the boundary, making documentation placement an operational rule.
techniques.quote:
Do not commit one-shot plans, trackers, migration ledgers, benchmark snapshots,
or agent scratch notes.

techniques.title: Attach logging changes to a dedicated skill
techniques.body: The root defines level semantics, reusable fields, and restrictions on sensitive data. It sends logging edits to a specific governance skill for the detailed workflow.

steal: Write precedence separately for local invariants and shared workflow.
Match verification to the effect of the final diff.
Allow no-findings reviews and require counterevidence checks.
Define which working notes belong outside the durable documentation.
